---
title: Pytest In Neovim
---

Many IDEs have extensions for running tests within them - for instance VS code
does a great job in doing this for `C#`. I wanted to make it easy to run tests
on my python code within `neovim` (since it is my preferred editor) to enhance
my productivity and determine if I can run my `C#` tests inside neovim instead
of VS code.

The plugins used here can be used with just about any language.

- Testing plugin: [Neotest](https://github.com/nvim-neotest/neotest?tab=readme-ov-file)
- Debugging plugin: [nvim-dap](https://github.com/mfussenegger/nvim-dap)

## Demo

The following will demonstrate how I use `neotest` to run tests inside of
neovim for `python`:

0. Enter the file you want to edit.

   ![Some silly tests open in neovim](img/open-tests-file.png)

   Additionally, I opened up the source file for the sake of this demo.

   ![Tests and code being tested.](img/open-tests-file-2.png)

1. Now start the tests for the entire file using `@@twe` in normal mode.
   This will open up the [`which-key`](https://github.com/folke/which-key)
   dialogue to show the options:

   ![Options after hitting `@@`](img/which-key-helper-0.png)

   ![Options after hitting `@@t`](img/which-key-helper-t.png)

   ![Options after hitting `@@tw`](img/which-key-helper-tw.png)

   This should open the test summary and output and run the tests:

   ![Result after running tests](img/tests-run.png)

2. First, we must make a test that fails since all of the tests pass initially.
   To do this we update `test_comprehension`. This will result in the tests
   re-running on `write`.

   ![Tests re-run after updating the test fail.](img/test-failed.png)

   To prove that we can go to a failing test, navigate to the top of the test
   file, then go back to a failing test using `@@tgfn`. This will open the
   test results just as shown above.

3. To enter a debug session, we just use `@@Db` to set the breakpoint where we
   want to enter and run `@@tcd` to run the closest test to the cursor. Then
   we can use `@@Di` to enter the debug session:

   ![Debug session in failed test](img/test-debug-0.png)

   Using the debug session it possible to see why our test failed:

   ![Debug session exploration.](img/test-debug-1.png)

## Configuration

## Key-maps

This is not exhaustive as there are many more specific
key-maps defined for tests, all of which can be explored using the
[`folke/which-key` plugin](https://github.com/folke/which-key) plugin as in
step 1.

```md
|       |                                     |
| ----- | ----------------------------------- |
| @@tf  | Run all tests in this file          |
| @@tfd | Test current value.                 |
| @@tc  | Run the closest tests to the cursor |
| @@tcd | Debug closest test.                 |
| @@tx  | Cancel tests.                       |
| @@ta  | To attach to test output.           |
| @@ts  | Test summary                        |
| @@to  | Show neotest output.                |
| @@tdb | Set/unset breakpoint                |
| @@tdc | Debug continue/exit                 |
| @@tdx | Exit the debug session              |
```
